Matching the formulation to the route

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A hospital pharmacy receives an order for intravenous acetylcysteine. A nearby vial contains sterile acetylcysteine solution labeled for inhalation or oral administration only. The concentration appears convenient for the ordered dose. Which action is most appropriate?

  1. Obtain the formulation approved for intravenous administration
  2. Use the inhalation vial because sterility guarantees intravenous suitability
  3. Inject the inhalation solution after dilution with saline
  4. Filter the inhalation solution and assume the route restriction is removed
  5. Change the ordered intravenous dose to the same volume of inhaled solution
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Obtain the formulation approved for intravenous administration

Products containing the same drug are not necessarily interchangeable across routes; inhalation/oral solution may explicitly prohibit injection.

Understanding the options

Obtain the formulation approved for intravenous administration
The correct formulation must be selected for the intended route.
Use the inhalation vial because sterility guarantees intravenous suitability
Sterility alone does not establish formulation suitability for injection.
Inject the inhalation solution after dilution with saline
Dilution does not override a not-for-injection label.
Filter the inhalation solution and assume the route restriction is removed
Filtering does not validate excipients or other formulation properties for intravenous use.
Change the ordered intravenous dose to the same volume of inhaled solution
Route and dose cannot be substituted by matching volume.
